title: What makes a generated character actually ready for your engine?
author: New-Still8833
selftext:
Before I bring a generated character into my game, I try the same quick checks each time. A neutral pose used to look good enough, until one shopkeeper folded badly during an animation test.



The base came from an image I ran through meshy. After cleaning the silhouette, I rigged and skinned it in my editor, then applied the same short test clip I use for characters from other sources. The elbows were acceptable, but the shoulder weight spread into the upper chest and pulled the collar sideways. I repainted that area twice; one pass fixed the collar but made the upper arm lose volume, and the next brought back a smaller crease.



Now my checklist starts with a few deliberately awkward poses: arms overhead, elbows fully bent, a deep crouch, and a torso twist. I watch for weight leaking across separate clothing pieces, collapsing joints, and vertices that lag behind the main limb. I would rather reject a mesh there than discover the issue while blocking a scene.



Which poses do you always test before bringing a character into the engine?

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: Iteration. Putting in engine the iterating and altering. However my pixel art chops are getting better and some of my enemies don’t need iteration once they are in engine but they usually do.
